sentiment.sum: XRP ~$1.31 (+1.1% 24h), defending $1.25. XRPL fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment activates ~23 Oct (bug fixes), but the lending protocol amendments are still short of votes (19-21 of 29), so lending likely slips to November. Ripple Prime's DTCC tokenization pilot is ongoing. Most buzz is price-target hype, ignored. Buzz cooling vs yesterday. Roughly neutral to mildly positive.

SUI back above $1.00 (+2.2% 24h) after weeks below it; Mysten Labs buybacks continue and the Hashi BTC-lending protocol is upcoming (no date). Much of the buzz is 'we're so back' price celebration after the reclaim, which is not counted as bullish news. Mildly positive at most.

HYPE ~$79.5 (+1.1% 24h). Kinetiq set Elysium L2 mainnet for 9 Nov (HYPE as gas). Mentions jumped sharply today (~15x yesterday's hourly rate), driven by the Elysium date and a story that retail wallet-app users lost ~$280M on Hyperliquid, mostly to fees. Price has not run, so this is news rather than post-pump hype, but the retail-loss angle and heavy leverage keep it near neutral.

ETH ~$2,421 (+0.3% 24h). Glamsterdam upgrade is set for 26 Oct (doubles gas limit to 200M), and JPMorgan opened JPM Coin to Ethereum mainnet. Against that, ETH ETFs lost ~$320M last week and a large 25x short sits near spot. Slightly positive on dated upgrade and institutional news, not price.

BTC ~$82.4k (+0.7% 24h), holding above the $81k support. Strategy filed a real buy today (267 BTC, plus a $3bn preferred buyback programme) and Strive added 1,223 BTC last week. Offsets: US BTC ETFs saw ~$229M outflows last week (third straight week), and MARA moved 1,000 BTC to exchanges. Long-term holders are sending far fewer coins to exchanges (CryptoQuant). Slightly more positive than this morning now the Strategy buy is confirmed.
BNB ~$728 (+0.7% 24h). BNB Chain completed its 37th quarterly burn (1.65M BNB, ~$1.2bn) and now holds ~43% of tokenized-stock supply. The burn is scheduled and expected, so modest positive.

XRP ~$1.31 (+1.3% 24h), buyers repeatedly defending $1.25. Ripple's Monica Long outlined using XRP as collateral for real-world credit on XRPL and Cross River Bank is integrating RLUSD with XRPL support; ETF inflows reported strong. Rising exchange reserves are a caution. Much of the buzz is price-target hype ($7-$50,000), which is ignored. Mildly positive.

World launched a World ID suite for banks and financial firms, with deepfake detection live on Zoom and a 'Proof of Human' badge; Bain Capital among testers. Real product news while price is flat (+0.4% 24h, ~$0.495) and mentions modest (~2.3k/24h), so this is news ahead of price rather than hype after a run. Positive.

TRON topped blockchain revenue rankings over 24h/7d/30d (~$23.4M monthly) and settled $2.21T of stablecoins in Q3; TRON Inc bought 149,576 TRX on 19 Oct (small). Price flat (-0.5% 24h). Quiet, fundamentals-led positive.

SOL ~$105.8 (+2.1% 24h) after dipping near $104. Ansem said he is cutting longs and derisking; others call it 'max bid territory'. Fundamentals still constructive (Western Union USDPT on Bitso, second HK spot SOL ETF) and the Alpenglow upgrade is due 21 Oct. Slightly less positive than last night given trader derisking.

Injective's real-world-asset perps passed $1.1B year-to-date volume (about $230M in the last 30 days) and the IIP-709 fixed-gas upgrade went live on 17 Oct. Price ~$8.60 (+0.9% 24h) with buzz below its mid-week levels. Mildly positive, no run-up.

ETH ~$2,432 (+0.9% 24h). A fresh 25x ETH short (~$21M left after partial liquidation) sits with liquidation ~$2,430, right at spot, so squeeze-or-dump volatility is likely. Vitalik pushed draft EIP-8288 (client-side STARK proofs) with no activation timeline, so not a catalyst. Alts still weak vs BTC dominance. Neutral.

BTC back near $82.8k (+1.4% 24h) after weekend lows near $80k, which traders treat as solid support. Bearish weekly engulfing (Ansem) points to $75k/$72k risk, but on-chain inflows are stabilising (Willy Woo), the US turned net BTC importer, Saylor teased another Strategy buy (not yet filed), and US futures opened higher despite 'Black Monday' chatter. Dominance ~60.8%, a 14-month high. Slightly positive vs last night.

Robinhood Chain, built on Arbitrum, passed $1.05B TVL on 18 Oct after ~100 days, with 1.58M real-world-asset holders. This is ecosystem news rather than an ARB token event. ARB is already +7.7% in 24h with buzz ~1.5x its last prints, so mild run-up caution.

ZEC fell ~8.8% in 24h to ~$1,057 after peaking above $1,200, with privacy coins amplifying the alt sell-off. Positive: Zcash shipped post-quantum unlinkable swap addresses; Burniske and Altcoin Sherpa frame sub-$1,000 as a buy zone. Bears eye $888 if support breaks. Mentions below the 3-day norm (0.83x). Mildly bearish short term.

XRP -3.2% in 24h to ~$1.26, down from >$1.40-1.50 earlier in October. Real items: Cross River Bank integrating RLUSD and the XRP Ledger, Ripple's Monica Long on XRP as payment-credit collateral, Evernorth's XRP treasury deployment. Rest is holder fatigue mixed with outsized price targets. Ripple/XRPL mentions are well below the 3-day norm (0.6x). Neutral, slight positive.

SOL -3.1% in 24h to ~$101 with the market. Fundamentals news is positive: Western Union's USDPT stablecoin is live on Bitso in Mexico, HKEX listed a second spot SOL ETF (Pando), record Q3 activity (14.2B txs, app revenue +48%), and the Alpenglow upgrade is due around 21 Oct (finality ~150ms). Mentions slightly below the 3-day norm. Mildly bullish on catalysts despite weak price.

MON -8.8% in 24h to ~$0.0201, below its public-sale price; posts say it lost $0.025 support. Community tone is frustrated (scam calls, 'where are the market makers'), and Monad TVL is falling with the native token. Several posts flag the large 24 Nov cliff unlock (~16.6B MON per one account, bigger than the circulating float). A few dip-buy calls. Bearish.

ETH -3.1% in 24h to ~$2,342, underperforming BTC as BTC dominance climbs to 60.8% and traders call it short-term bearish for alts. ETH-specific talk is mostly the lattice vs hash post-quantum debate and NFT activity; nothing price-moving. Mentions slightly below the 3-day norm. Mildly bearish.

BTC eased from ~$87k highs to ~$80.8k (-0.9% 24h). Dominance hit 60.8%, a 1-year high. Weekly ETF outflows ~$228M, over $321M of liquidations in 24h (mostly longs), and 'Black Monday' chatter ahead of the US open on 19 Oct after a weekend sell-off in tokenized chip stocks. Offsets: Saylor teasing another Strategy buy, a $110M 40x long on Hyperliquid near $81.9k (liquidation ~$80k). Slightly bearish into Monday.

STRK is down about 12% in 24h and roughly 40-46% on the week, as the 127M-token unlock on 15 Oct works through. StarkWare's non-binding poll (open until 22 Oct) shows 99.95% support for researching an independent post-quantum L1, but any move is years away, and posts say supply is still being absorbed. Mildly bearish.

Solana reported a record Q3: app revenue up 48% to $299M, 14.2B transactions and $7.1B in tokenized equities volume. The Alpenglow upgrade, targeting 150ms finality, is flagged for 21 Oct. Price is flat around $104 and mentions are below the norm (0.8x), so this is quiet strength, not hype. Mildly bullish.

An early HYPE whale has been selling, including about $8.2M of HYPE sent to Kraken, locking in over $21M profit. Price is flat near $79. Buyback-and-burn support is unchanged, but visible whale distribution tempers the outlook. Mentions are below the 3-day norm (0.8x). Neutral.

HBAR is up about 7% in 24h and trending on X, but the story is chart talk (double bottom, resistance at $0.088) plus unverified whale-accumulation claims, with no dated catalyst. Mentions are about 1.5x the 3-day norm on a coin that has already run, so treat it as overheating, not news. Neutral.

BTC is flat around $81-82k in a $74-88k range. Bullish on-chain and institutional talk is offset by a weekend sell-off in tokenized chip stocks and 'Black Monday' chatter ahead of the US open on 19 Oct. France's narrow vote to tax crypto-to-stablecoin swaps from 2027 is still pending Senate review. Mixed, neutral.

Monero is +6.5% in 24h and was one of only two large coins up on the week. No dated news: overnight X volume is inflated by copy-paste 'vote for $Monero on CoinMarketCap' spam tied to an unrelated token contract, so raw counts overstate interest; the 24h total is about 0.84x the 3-day norm. FCMP upgrade talk is ongoing, with no release date. Neutral.

SAND is +24% in 24h, but X chatter about The Sandbox is flat (about 1.0x its 3-day norm), so this is a quiet move rather than a hype spike. The only project item is Sandbox Studio, its AI game builder, opening to the public later this month after closed testing (no firm date). Some posts link it to a gaming-token rotation (MAGIC, PIXEL). Gainer-list posts ignored. Mildly positive, but the move is already large.

The only US spot Hedera ETF had a $559K net outflow on 17 Oct, only its second outflow day, though it still holds about 1.81% of supply. Some posts say Karate Combat is ending its Hedera tie-up (not confirmed). Price is still +4.7% in 24h on flat buzz (about 1.06x norm). Slightly negative.

Bitway is +26% in 24h and about +60% over 7 days, with no verified catalyst found (one trader explicitly notes none). Mentions are cooling (about 0.7x the 3-day norm), so this is not a buzz spike, and a few posts call it a pump. Neutral: strong tape, no news to back it.

New since morning: Ripple-backed Evernorth, which holds 473M XRP, is now listed on Nasdaq as XRPN and plans to deploy its treasury. Cross River RLUSD news already counted. The rest of tonight's XRP talk is $750-$1,000 price-target hype, ignored. Price ~$1.30, -2.5% 24h. Raw X counts spiked in three hours again (same pattern as the morning's phishing-bot flood); organic hours run ~0.85x the 3-day norm. Mildly positive.

New tonight: Pentiv (ex-Pineapple Financial) says it has tokenized over $1B of mortgage records on Injective and aims to move its full $10B, 29,000-loan book there; its $100M INJ treasury has earned ~$399K staking. Real-world-asset use, not hype. Price ~$8.69, +2% 24h, so no run-up; buzz ~1.2x norm. Mildly positive.

HYPE broke supports and fell to ~$79 (-3% 24h, from above $85 earlier this month), and traders are piling into large leveraged shorts on Hyperliquid. Buzz is up ~1.3x its norm while the price falls, which is fear rather than a run-up. Pump.fun perps integration from the morning still stands. Down from +0.20 to roughly neutral.

New tonight: Bitfinex margin longs hit a record 367.5k ETH (~$889M), up more than 300% this October, so big traders are leaning long; that is positioning, not a dated event, and crowded longs cut both ways. ETF outflow news already counted at midday. Price ~$2,417, -1% 24h; buzz ~1.0x its 3-day norm. Close to neutral, a touch positive.

BitTorrent completed its first revenue-funded quarterly buyback-and-burn on 17 Oct, removing ~21.6T BTT (about 2.18% of supply) on TRON. That is a dated supply event. Buzz is up ~1.5x its 3-day norm but the price has barely moved (+0.5% 24h), so this is not chasing a pump. Mildly positive.

Numerai launched 'Unity' (16 Oct): a dataset with real stock identifiers and 1,040 features, merging Numerai and Numerai Signals into one meta-model for AI agents. Official announcement; buzz small but ~2.3x normal. Price +5.6% 24h. Positive.

variants.ev_note: EV exit is off. Live expected value rises when the trade falls, because the upside is the distance to the stored target and the chance is not recomputed, so a negative reading is a winner. ev_exit, all_combined and everything were reset; sells before the reset are not counted. The exit stays off until the upside is taken from the current price and the chance is recomputed.

books.name: main
books.label: Main book
books.blurb: Frozen rules. This is the book the cycle commits.

books.name: ev_exit
books.label: EV exit
books.blurb: EV exit is off. Live expected value rises when the trade falls, so it was selling winners between about +1% and +5%. This book was reset; sells before the reset are not counted. It follows the main book until the upside is taken from the current price and the chance is recomputed.

books.name: review_leftovers
books.label: Review leftovers
books.blurb: Burst stop is 1.5x wider unless live EV is already below -0.4%. Core's 18:00 fallback tranche is half size when the coin is up more than 15% over 7 days or RSI is above 75. New Day, Risk and Core entries need the coin's own 3-day trend up. After 12:00 UK, Day and Core will not each buy the same coin.

books.name: all_combined
books.label: Both together
books.blurb: The review leftovers, on one book. The EV exit is off (live expected value was inverted) and this book was reset; sells before the reset are not counted. The burst runner is a separate book, not part of this one.

books.name: burst_runner
books.label: Burst runner
books.blurb: Same rules as the main book, except a Burst position that hits its target keeps running when the entry signal is still intact. The trail then gives back 20% of the peak gain. Each sell says sold at target or ran, with the extra gain and the giveback.

books.name: everything
books.label: Everything combined
books.blurb: The review leftovers and the burst runner, on one book. The EV exit is off (live expected value was inverted) and this book was reset; sells before the reset are not counted.

books.name: midnight_crypto
books.label: Midnight crypto
books.blurb: Same as the main book, except Day crypto entries run until 23:45 UK and those positions flatten at 00:00 UK. New crypto entries are allowed again from 00:00, and the daily loss budget still resets then. Stocks still flatten 15 minutes before their market closes. Copied from the same snapshot as the other books.

books.name: entry_watch
books.label: Entry watch
books.blurb: Same scoring as the main book. Setups the cycle would buy are also armed with a price trigger, a size, and the same stop and target. This is the only book the live watcher is allowed to buy when that trigger trades between cycles. The main book only logs those as WOULD BUY.

books.name: risk_giveback_15
books.label: Risk giveback 15
books.blurb: Risk only. The trail still arms at +15% net. Once armed, it sells when the net gain falls to 65% of the peak net gain, and the 7-day exit waits while that trail is armed. The -12% stop stays. Not combined with the other paper books.

books.name: day_trail_arm
books.label: Day trail arm
books.blurb: Day only. A trail arms only when 60% of the peak gain is at least the greater of 4x that trade's round-trip cost and 1x its 1-hour ATR. Once armed, a crossed trail sells. Stop, target, the burst 6-hour hold and the 22:00 flatten stay.

books.name: day_ev_blend
books.label: Day EV blend
books.blurb: Day only. Each sub-strategy's expected value is its measured expectancy blended with the model: (n x measured + 10 x model) / (n + 10). Momentum and burst are measured apart. The Risk win is not changed on this book.

books.name: no_risk_clock
books.label: No risk clock
books.blurb: Risk only. The 24-hour re-entry clock is deleted. The next setup buys when its own confidence and expected value clear. No new-high gate and no stop-out cooldown.

books.name: day_capital_caution
books.label: Day capital caution
books.blurb: Day only, per account. f is that account's Day loss today divided by 15% of that account's start-of-day Day equity, with no cap at 1. Momentum's threshold is its base (0.35, or 0.30 on MON, WLD and XRP) plus 0.30 x f. Burst uses the same f. Size is multiplied by (1 - min(f, 1)). The -15% halt on the whole Day pot stays.

books.name: partial_take
books.label: Partial take
books.blurb: Day and Risk. At the trail arm, sell half and leave the rest on this book's trail. Buy that half back on a later dip only when a fresh expected value clears the hurdle. The fresh value uses a recomputed chance and the percent still available from the current price, not the inverted live EV. Orders in this split may be £1. Every other book keeps the £5 minimum. The sell records the extra fee of splitting one exit into two.

books.name: sent_split
books.label: Sentiment split
books.blurb: Burst and Risk. A missing sentiment print scores 0.50, the same as a real neutral, instead of 0.25. A Risk dip needs the 48-hour uptrend; positive sentiment does not stand in for it. When price is up 15% or more over 24 hours (5% or more over 4 hours on a Day momentum entry) and sentiment is at least 0.30, or the buzz change is 3 or more, burst and Risk confidence lose 0.10 and that Day momentum entry ignores sentiment. A catalyst score, when the file has one, is used instead of the raw score. A quiet tape (buzz change under 1.2) with volume at least 2x and a confirmed breakout or bounce adds 0.05. Files without those fields score as before.

books.name: best_of
books.label: Best of
books.blurb: Sentiment split, the entry watcher and the burst runner, and nothing else. A missing sentiment print is neutral (0.50). A Risk dip needs the 48-hour uptrend. Hot run-up and quiet-tape adjustments are the sentiment-split numbers. Armed entries expire after 15 minutes. A burst that hits its target can keep running and then gives back 20% of the peak gain. The EV exit stays off.

books.name: btc_trend
books.label: BTC trend
books.blurb: Crypto is 100% BTC when the daily close is above its 50-day average, otherwise cash. Stocks is the same rule on VUSA, or EQQQ if VUSA has no history. Checked once a day. Held through nights and weekends.

books.name: btc_trend_vol
books.label: BTC trend, vol sized
books.blurb: The same trend book, sized at min(1, 40% / 30-day realised vol). A weight only moves when it has drifted more than 5 points.

strategies.label: Main book
strategies.blurb: Frozen rules. This is the book the cycle commits.

strategies.name: day_ev_blend
strategies.label: Day EV blend
strategies.blurb: Day only. Each sub-strategy's expected value is its measured expectancy blended with the model: (n x measured + 10 x model) / (n + 10). Momentum and burst are measured apart. The Risk win is not changed on this book.

strategies.name: day_capital_caution
strategies.label: Day capital caution
strategies.blurb: Day only, per account. f is that account's Day loss today divided by 15% of that account's start-of-day Day equity, with no cap at 1. Momentum's threshold is its base (0.35, or 0.30 on MON, WLD and XRP) plus 0.30 x f. Burst uses the same f. Size is multiplied by (1 - min(f, 1)). The -15% halt on the whole Day pot stays.

strategies.name: partial_take
strategies.label: Partial take

The fresh value uses a recomputed chance and the percent still available from the current price, not the inverted live EV. Orders in this split may be £1. Every other book keeps the £5 minimum. The sell records the extra fee of splitting one exit into two.

strategies.name: entry_watch
strategies.label: Entry watch
strategies.blurb: Same scoring as the main book. Setups the cycle would buy are also armed with a price trigger, a size, and the same stop and target. This is the only book the live watcher is allowed to buy when that trigger trades between cycles. The main book only logs those as WOULD BUY.

strategies.name: risk_giveback_15

strategies.name: no_risk_clock

strategies.name: all_combined
strategies.label: Both together

strategies.name: sent_split
strategies.label: Sentiment split
strategies.blurb: Burst and Risk. A missing sentiment print scores 0.50, the same as a real neutral, instead of 0.25. A Risk dip needs the 48-hour uptrend; positive sentiment does not stand in for it. When price is up 15% or more over 24 hours (5% or more over 4 hours on a Day momentum entry) and sentiment is at least 0.30, or the buzz change is 3 or more, burst and Risk confidence lose 0.10 and that Day momentum entry ignores sentiment. A catalyst score, when the file has one, is used instead of the raw score. A quiet tape (buzz change under 1.2) with volume at least 2x and a confirmed breakout or bounce adds 0.05. Files without those fields score as before.

strategies.name: best_of
strategies.label: Best of
strategies.blurb: Sentiment split, the entry watcher and the burst runner, and nothing else. A missing sentiment print is neutral (0.50). A Risk dip needs the 48-hour uptrend. Hot run-up and quiet-tape adjustments are the sentiment-split numbers. Armed entries expire after 15 minutes. A burst that hits its target can keep running and then gives back 20% of the peak gain. The EV exit stays off.

strategies.name: day_trail_arm
strategies.label: Day trail arm
strategies.blurb: Day only. A trail arms only when 60% of the peak gain is at least the greater of 4x that trade's round-trip cost and 1x its 1-hour ATR. Once armed, a crossed trail sells. Stop, target, the burst 6-hour hold and the 22:00 flatten stay.

strategies.name: midnight_crypto
strategies.label: Midnight crypto
strategies.blurb: Same as the main book, except Day crypto entries run until 23:45 UK and those positions flatten at 00:00 UK. New crypto entries are allowed again from 00:00, and the daily loss budget still resets then. Stocks still flatten 15 minutes before their market closes. Copied from the same snapshot as the other books.

rulebook.name: main
rulebook.label: Main rules
rulebook.holds: Two accounts that never mix: £100 in crypto and £100 in stocks at the Test 2 start. Each account is split Core £50, Day £30 and Risk £20. Core holds longer growth names. Day holds two intraday books, momentum and burst, sharing that pot. Risk holds smaller speculative names. A pot may lend cash to another pot in the same account. Cash never crosses between the crypto account and the stock account.
rulebook.entry: Core adds to a name in daily slices after the weekly pick. Day momentum may buy from 08:00 UK when the score and the expected value after costs both clear, and it does not buy at or after 21:00. Burst buys a breakout that has enough volume. Risk buys a breakout, or a dip that has already bounced while the trend is still up. A name that is still falling is skipped. Less cash raises the hurdle and cuts the size. It does not halt the book.
rulebook.exit: Core sells a position that is 20% under its cost. There is no Core target; the weekly pick trims a winner. Day momentum uses a stop of about 2% to 5% and a target of about 4% to 12%, then a trail. Burst is tighter and also exits after 6 hours. Every Day position is sold at 22:00 UK, and a stock is sold 15 minutes before its market closes. A 15% loss on the Day pot stops new Day buys for the rest of that day. Risk sells at a 12% stop, or 10% under the peak after a 15% gain, or after 7 days. A 30% drop in the Risk pot stops new Risk buys.
rulebook.rebalance: Core picks again on Monday at 09:00 UK. Day does not hold a basket overnight, so it does not rebalance one. Risk does not rebalance; each position is its own trade.
rulebook.data: Live prices from Kraken, Coinbase, KyberSwap and Yahoo, a pound-dollar rate, Monad gas, and the sentiment file scored from news and X. A price that is getting old lowers confidence. It does not by itself block a sell.
rulebook.tweak: The frozen Core, Day and Risk rules. Every other row in this group changes one of them.

rulebook.name: signal_funding_carry
rulebook.label: Funding carry
rulebook.holds: BTC, or cash. The stock half stays in cash.
rulebook.entry: Once a week, hold BTC only when yesterday's annualised perpetual funding is hot: 25% a year, or above the prior year's 90th percentile.
rulebook.exit: Cash when funding is not hot. No funding history means cash.
rulebook.rebalance: Once a week. The position is all or nothing.
rulebook.data: The same lagged Deribit funding cache as the cash-when-hot book. This is the opposite sign.

rulebook.name: signal_basis
rulebook.label: Basis, cash when rich
rulebook.holds: BTC, or cash. The stock half stays in cash.
rulebook.entry: Once a week, hold BTC when the previous 7-day perp premium is not rich.
rulebook.exit: Cash when that premium is above its trailing median. No history means cash.
rulebook.rebalance: Once a week. The position is all or nothing.
rulebook.data: Deribit BTC perpetual close over the BTC spot close, lagged. Shared cache.

rulebook.name: signal_dvol
rulebook.label: DVOL fear
rulebook.holds: BTC, or cash. The stock half stays in cash.
rulebook.entry: Once a week, hold BTC when the previous Deribit volatility index is not in the top of its own past year.
rulebook.exit: Cash when that index is above its trailing 252-day 80th percentile. No history means cash.
rulebook.rebalance: Once a week. The position is all or nothing.
rulebook.data: Deribit DVOL, lagged one day. Shared cache.

rulebook.name: signal_vrp
rulebook.label: Variance premium
rulebook.holds: BTC, or cash. The stock half stays in cash.
rulebook.entry: Once a week, hold BTC when implied variance minus 30-day realised variance is above its trailing median.
rulebook.exit: Cash when that premium is not above the median. No history means cash.
rulebook.rebalance: Once a week. The position is all or nothing.
rulebook.data: Deribit DVOL and BTC daily closes. Realised variance from daily closes is a coarse stand-in for a high-frequency measure.

rulebook.name: signal_stablecoin
rulebook.label: Stablecoin supply
rulebook.holds: BTC, or cash. The stock half stays in cash.
rulebook.entry: Once a week, hold BTC when the lagged 30-day change in stablecoin supply is positive.
rulebook.exit: Cash when that change is not positive. No history means cash. This is a hypothesis, not a published result.
rulebook.rebalance: Once a week. The position is all or nothing.
rulebook.data: Stablecoin supply, lagged one day. Shared cache.

rulebook.name: signal_macro
rulebook.label: Macro permission
rulebook.holds: BTC in the crypto half and VUSA in the stock half, each on its own, or cash.
rulebook.entry: Once a week, a sleeve is invested only when the Nasdaq is above its 200-day average and the dollar index is down over 50 days.
rulebook.exit: That sleeve is cash when either condition fails. Missing market data leaves both sleeves in cash.
rulebook.rebalance: Once a week. Each sleeve is all or nothing.
rulebook.data: Nasdaq and the dollar index, lagged one day, plus BTC and VUSA closes. Shared cache.

rulebook.name: signal_tsmom
rulebook.label: 12-month momentum
rulebook.holds: BTC, and VUSA on its own price. Either sleeve can be cash.
rulebook.entry: Once a month, hold the asset when its 12-month return, skipping the most recent month, is positive.
rulebook.exit: Cash for that sleeve when the return is not positive.
rulebook.rebalance: Once a month. A weekend does not sell the stock sleeve just because the market is closed.
rulebook.data: BTC and VUSA daily closes only. No extra feed.

rulebook.name: signal_gold
rulebook.label: Gold risk-on
rulebook.holds: BTC, or cash. The stock half stays in cash.
rulebook.entry: Once a month, hold BTC when the lagged 126-day gold return is negative.
rulebook.exit: Cash when gold is not down over that window. No gold history means cash. This is a hypothesis.
rulebook.rebalance: Once a month. The position is all or nothing.
rulebook.data: Gold daily closes, lagged one day. Shared cache.

rulebook.name: signal_onchain
rulebook.label: Active addresses
rulebook.holds: BTC, or cash. The stock half stays in cash.
rulebook.entry: Once a week, hold BTC when the lagged 30-day change in unique Bitcoin addresses is positive.
rulebook.exit: Cash when that change is not positive. No history means cash. This is a hypothesis.
rulebook.rebalance: Once a week. The position is all or nothing.
rulebook.data: Unique Bitcoin addresses, lagged one day. Shared cache.

rulebook.name: signal_gdelt
rulebook.label: News tone
rulebook.holds: BTC, or cash. The stock half stays in cash.
rulebook.entry: Once a week, hold BTC when the previous 7-day average news tone for Bitcoin is positive.
rulebook.exit: Cash when that tone is not positive. No tone history means cash.
rulebook.rebalance: Once a week. The position is all or nothing.
rulebook.data: GDELT tone, lagged so the week used ends the day before the decision. Shared cache. Separate from the hourly headline file.

rulebook.name: signal_dominance
rulebook.label: BTC dominance
rulebook.holds: BTC, or cash. The stock half stays in cash.
rulebook.entry: Once a week, hold BTC when lagged 30-day BTC dominance rose.
rulebook.exit: Cash when dominance did not rise over those 30 days. No history means cash. This is a hypothesis.
rulebook.rebalance: Once a week. The position is all or nothing.
rulebook.data: BTC share of crypto market cap, lagged one day. Shared cache.

rulebook.name: ev_exit
rulebook.label: EV exit
rulebook.tweak: Would sell when live expected value turns negative. That rule is off: the live number rose as the trade fell. This book was reset and now follows the main rules.

rulebook.name: review_leftovers
rulebook.label: Review leftovers
rulebook.tweak: Wider burst stop, a smaller Core fallback when a coin is extended, a 3-day uptrend on a new entry, and no Day plus Core buy of the same coin after midday.

rulebook.name: all_combined
rulebook.label: Both together
rulebook.tweak: The review leftovers on one book. The burst runner is not part of this one.

rulebook.name: burst_runner
rulebook.label: Burst runner
rulebook.tweak: A burst that hits its target keeps running, then gives back 20% of the peak gain.

rulebook.name: everything
rulebook.label: Everything combined
rulebook.tweak: The review leftovers and the burst runner, together.

rulebook.name: midnight_crypto
rulebook.label: Midnight crypto
rulebook.tweak: Day crypto may enter until 23:45 UK and flattens at midnight. Stocks still flatten before the close.

rulebook.name: entry_watch
rulebook.label: Entry watch
rulebook.tweak: Buys between cycles when an armed price trigger trades. The main book only logs that as a would-buy.

rulebook.name: risk_giveback_15
rulebook.label: Risk giveback 15
rulebook.tweak: After a Risk trade is up 15%, sell when the gain falls to 65% of the peak gain.

rulebook.name: day_trail_arm
rulebook.label: Day trail arm
rulebook.tweak: A Day trail arms only when 60% of the peak gain clears the round-trip cost and the 1-hour range.

rulebook.name: day_ev_blend
rulebook.label: Day EV blend
rulebook.tweak: A Day entry's expected value blends the model with that sleeve's own measured results.

rulebook.name: no_risk_clock
rulebook.label: No risk clock
rulebook.tweak: Risk may re-enter the same name without waiting 24 hours.

rulebook.name: day_capital_caution
rulebook.label: Day capital caution
rulebook.tweak: A losing Day account raises the entry hurdle and cuts size. The 15% halt on the Day pot stays.

rulebook.name: partial_take
rulebook.label: Partial take
rulebook.tweak: At the trail arm, sell half. Buy that half back on a dip only when a fresh expected value clears.

rulebook.name: sent_split
rulebook.label: Sentiment split
rulebook.tweak: Missing sentiment counts as neutral. A hot run-up is penalised, and a quiet tape can earn a small bonus.

rulebook.name: best_of
rulebook.label: Best of
rulebook.tweak: Sentiment split, the 15-minute entry watch, and the burst runner, together. No other main-rule change.

rows.label: News

rows.label: Routine file
rows.blurb: The sentiment file the cycle already ingests, from -1 to 1.

rows.label: Funding
rows.blurb: Low BTC perpetual funding is the bullish reading. High funding is negative.

rows.label: Unlocks
rows.blurb: No large unlock is the bullish reading. A token unlocking supply is negative.

rows.label: Insider buys
rows.blurb: An opportunistic open-market insider buy in the last six months.

rows.label: Trend
rows.blurb: 1 when the close is above its 50-day average, otherwise -1.

rows.label: Momentum
rows.blurb: The last 28-day return, shrunk so a 20% move is the full score.

rows.label: Volatility
rows.blurb: Calm volatility is bullish. A realised vol of 40% is neutral and 80% is -1.

rows.label: 5-day forecast
rows.blurb: Half of the last 5-day return, shrunk. Kept only when that has predicted the next week.

engine.note: A signal is used only when an older window and a later window agree on its rank correlation with the next five daily returns, and neither correlation is tiny or perfect. The weight is the weaker of those two. News is scored by a finance lexicon, hourly, outside this cycle.
